steps.tx: Although testosterone is the principal circulating androgen in males, its biological potency is amplified in specific target tissues through enzymatic conversion into **dihydrotestosterone**. Dihydrotestosterone binds the intracellular androgen receptor with twofold greater affinity and dissociates fivefold more slowly than testosterone.
steps.say: Dihydrotestosterone binds androgen receptors twice as tightly as testosterone, amplifying androgen signals in target tissues.

left.title: Testosterone Direct Actions
points: Differentiation of internal Wolffian duct structures (epididymis, vas)
Skeletal muscle hypertrophy and nitrogen retention at puberty
Stimulation of erythropoiesis in bone marrow
Deepening of vocal cords and pubertal growth spurt

right.title: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT) Actions
points: Differentiation of external male genitalia (penis, scrotum)
Prostate gland growth and secretory development
Temporal hairline recession and male pattern baldness
Sebaceous gland activity and pubertal acne

steps.tx: The enzymatic conversion of testosterone to dihydrotestosterone is catalyzed in target tissues by the microsomal enzyme **five-alpha reductase**. This key enzyme irreversibly reduces the double bond between carbons four and five on the A-ring of the steroid nucleus using NADPH as an essential electron donor.
steps.say: Five-alpha reductase converts testosterone into dihydrotestosterone in the prostate, skin, and hair follicles.

rows: Involved in adult sebum production and acne
Required for fetal external male differentiation; target in BPH

steps.tx: During embryonic development, male sexual differentiation depends upon coordinated hormonal secretion by the fetal testes. Fetal Leydig cell testosterone drives the stabilization and morphological differentiation of the **internal Wolffian duct structures**, including the embryonic epididymides, paired vasa deferentia, and seminal vesicles.
steps.say: Testosterone differentiates internal Wolffian structures, while anti-Mullerian hormone regresses female internal ducts.

nodes.label: SRY Gene on Y Chromosome Directs Primitive Gonadal Ridge to Differentiate into Testis
Sertoli Cells Secrete Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) -> Regresses Müllerian Ducts
Leydig Cells Secrete Testosterone -> Differentiates Wolffian Ducts (Vas, Epididymis)
5-Alpha Reductase Converts Testosterone to DHT -> Differentiates External Genitalia

steps.tx: Simultaneously, Sertoli cells secrete anti-Müllerian hormone, causing regression of the paramesonephric Müllerian ducts. In the external urogenital sinus and genital tubercle, local five-alpha reductase converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone, driving development of the **external male genitalia**, including the penis, penile urethra, and scrotum.
steps.say: Local conversion to DHT differentiates external male genitalia like the penis, scrotum, and prostate.

left.title: Internal Duct Differentiation
points: Mediated directly by high local concentrations of Testosterone
Wolffian duct develops into epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicles

right.title: External Genital Virilization
points: Genital tubercle expands to form glans and shaft of penis
Urogenital folds fuse to enclose penile urethra
Labioscrotal swellings fuse in the midline to form the scrotum

steps.tx: Inherited autosomal recessive deficiency of type 2 five-alpha reductase produces **five-alpha reductase deficiency**, a classic cause of 46,XY differences of sex development. Affected infants are born with ambiguous or female-appearing external genitalia alongside normal male internal Wolffian structures and non-palpable undescended testes.
steps.say: Five-alpha reductase deficiency causes female-appearing genitalia at birth, virilizing dramatically into male form at puberty.

nodes.label: Infant Born with Ambiguous Genitalia (Clitoromegaly, Bifid Scrotum, Blind Vaginal Pouch)
Internal Anatomy: Normal Male Vasa Deferentia and Epididymides (Testosterone-Driven)
Pubertal Surge of Pituitary LH Produces Massive Elevation of Circulating Testosterone
Type 1 5-Alpha Reductase and High Testosterone Drive Dramatic Virilization and Penile Growth

steps.tx: At puberty, the massive surge in pituitary luteinizing hormone produces exceptionally high circulating testosterone levels that engage androgen receptors directly and undergo conversion via hepatic type 1 five-alpha reductase. Consequently, patients undergo dramatic **pubertal male virilization**, marked by phallic elongation, deepening voice, and testicular descent.
steps.say: Massive pubertal testosterone surges virilize patients with five-alpha reductase deficiency, triggering phallic enlargement.

steps.tx: In adult men, dihydrotestosterone promotes benign hyperplasia of glandular and stromal elements in the prostatic transition zone, causing **benign prostatic hyperplasia**. Progressively compressing the prostatic urethra, benign prostatic hyperplasia causes lower urinary tract symptoms, including weak stream, nocturia, urinary hesitancy, and incomplete emptying.
steps.say: In older men, DHT stimulates prostate stromal growth, causing benign prostatic hyperplasia and urinary obstruction.

steps.tx: Pharmacological inhibition of five-alpha reductase with **finasteride and dutasteride** slashes circulating and intraprostatic dihydrotestosterone concentrations by seventy to ninety percent. By eliminating the trophic DHT stimulus, these agents induce prostatic epithelial apoptosis, shrinking prostate volume by twenty-five percent and halting androgenic alopecia.
steps.say: Finasteride blocks five-alpha reductase, shrinking enlarged prostates by a quarter and halting male pattern baldness.
